note.en: Landmarks to confirm: Arch of aorta

steps.en: What you see: The arch curves like a walking stick with the ascending limb in front and the descending limb behind. Three branches leave the top in order: brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian.
Landmarks to confirm: Do not accept the view until each of these is on screen.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Each mistake below comes from the view catalogue with its correction.
Normal values and stenosis thresholds: Peak aortic velocity above 4 m per s means severe stenosis.
Mean transaortic gradient above 40 mmHg means severe stenosis.
Aortic valve area below 1.0 sq cm means severe stenosis.
Report the highest velocity from any window: apical, suprasternal or right parasternal.

Pitfalls: A tortuous innominate artery can mimic a dissection flap at a branch mouth; confirm any flap in short axis. In coarctation look for diastolic runoff continuing through diastole in the descending limb.

analogy.en: Landmarks to confirm: Arch of aorta

spot.en: Landmarks to confirm: Arch of aorta

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Left carotid mistaken for the arch apex so length is understated. Correct it by following the curve until three branches leave it, since the carotid gives none.
Lung shadowing the proximal arch in systole. Correct it by waiting for held breath out and pressing a touch firmer.
Too lateral a window that loses the descending limb. Correct it by returning to the midline notch and starting again.

todo.en: How to get it: Place the probe at suprasternal notch, sagittal with neck extended.
Point the probe marker toward the head, about twelve o clock.
Extend the neck with a pillow under the shoulders and press sagittal in the notch. If lung blocks the proximal arch, ask for a held breath out.
Freeze the image only when every listed landmark is on screen at once.

remember.en: Take the suprasternal Doppler line for aortic stenosis.

q.en: Name the arch branches in order from the ascending limb.

o.en: Brachiocephalic, left common carotid, left subclavian

why.en: The brachiocephalic trunk comes first, then left carotid, then left subclavian.

q.en: Apical velocity is 3.5 m per s but suprasternal is 4.3 m per s. Which counts?

why.en: Grading uses the highest clean envelope from any window.

q.en: Colour continues through diastole in the descending limb of a young hypertensive patient. What is suspected?

why.en: Diastolic runoff in the descending aorta points to coarctation.
